newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Bass half-year profit rises 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bass half-year profit rises 10 pct.

text.p: British brewer to hotel group Bass Plc, reporting a 10 percent rise in half-year profits, said on Wednesday that conditions in Germany and France had reached their low point and were now on their way back up.

Chairman Sir Ian Prosser talked in positive terms about the group's markets, describing them as robust and healthy after reporting profit before tax of 318 million pounds ($526.2 million), up from 289 million a year earlier.

"Germany and France have probably bottomed out and are now on the way back up and in America we are continuing to see good economic growth. We are seeing most central banks taking action against inflation," Prosser told Reuters.

Bass hopes the new British Labour government will reach a decision on the group's proposed acquisition of brewer Carlsberg-Tetley in the middle of next month. "I would guess mid-June we might hear," said Prosser.

Labour is widely expected to impose more stringent conditions on the merger than the former Conservative government or even block it altogether. The merger would create Britain's largest brewer with a 35 percent share of the market. Uncertainty over the outcome of Bass's bid for C-T has continued to depress its share price.
Bass shares were off 13 pence at 808 by late morning.

Asked what other uncertainties a change of government brought for the group, Prosser said: "Their attitude over a minimum wage and where they would set that. I think it should be set at a relatively low figure and phased in over a period of time to give companies a chance to accommodate it."

Britain's largest trade union, UNISON, representing 1.3 million public sector workers, is asking the government to impose a minimum wage of 4.42 pounds an hour. Labour plans to set up a Low Pay Commission to take evidence from employers and unions before recommending a minimum wage.
The introduction of a minimum wage is likely to affect the food, drink and retail sector, especially given the high number of part time, low-paid staff employed.

Peter Jarvis, chief executive of Whitbread Plc until June 2 when he is tipped to head up the Low Pay unit, has called for a minimum wage to be applied on a regional basis and to take account of incentive schemes offered by companies and training costs.
Bass employs about 70,000 people, including 50,000 in its British pubs, most of them as bar staff.
Bass said the profits rise was driven by its managed pubs and 2,200 Holiday Inn hotel empire.

Prosser said the company should add a total 200 managed pubs by the year end, after adding in 83 in the first half. The group's pub outlets include Harvester restaurants, O'Neill's Irish bars and Vintage Inns.

Group capital expenditure will be reduced to 620 million pounds for the year as a whole from an original forecast of 750 million, said Prosser. This was mainly because the acquisition of 60 Holiday Inns in North America by the Bristol Hotel Company means Bass no longer needs to spend on maintaining them.

The Bass-owned Gala chain of bingo halls, the one area of weakness in the group's half year results, was being looked at hard and management had been changed, said Prosser. Gala's trading profit fell 6.0 million pounds to 13 million in the half year as competition intensified and more new clubs opened up.
Brokers had forecast overall profits of between 305 and 325 million pounds. The dividend payout was also in line with expectations at 8.3 pence per share.

Group turnover grew by 6.8 percent to 2.693 billion pounds. Holiday Inn's improved operating profit 5.3 percent to 80 million pounds, or 10.2 percent in dollar terms as average room rates in America rose sharply.

Bass' 2,812 managed pubs raised trading profits by 12.6 percent to 116 million pounds while the group's leisure division, which includes Gala and Coral betting shops, raised profits by 11.4 percent to 39 million.

Profits from the beer business were 6.9 percent higher in the first half of 1997 than in 1996 at 77 million pounds, with key brands Carling Black Label and Worthington draught bitter performing strongly.
($ = 0.604 British Pounds)
